beats.label: PRICE ÷ EARNINGS  ·  P/E
beats.title: How many years until $100 pays you back?
beats.caption: Each coin is one year of earnings on $100 of stock (last 12 months). KO pays it back in 25 years, AAPL in 35 and NVDA in 51. INTC is losing money, so at these earnings it never does.

beats.label: MARKET VALUE vs. PROFIT
beats.title: The building and its rent
beats.caption: Height is market value, all on one scale. Each floor is one year of profit: the rent the building collects. NVDA is tallest at $4.39T, 51 floors high. INTC collects no rent right now.

beats.label: EARNINGS, FREE CASH FLOW AND DIVIDEND YIELD
beats.title: What $100 of stock earns in a year
beats.caption: KO earns the most per $100 ($4.00 a year) and pays the most out in cash ($2.91). For scale: 10-yr Treasury, $4.20.

beats.label: GROSS → OPERATING → NET MARGIN
beats.title: What's left of every $100 of sales
beats.caption: After the cost of the product, running the business, interest and tax: NVDA keeps $52, KO keeps $26, AAPL keeps $25 and INTC loses $36.

beats.label: FORWARD P/E vs. EXPECTED GROWTH  ·  PEG
beats.title: The price of growth
beats.caption: Higher means paying more for each dollar of next year's earnings. Further right means faster expected growth. Each dashed line is one PEG (P/E ÷ growth). Bubble area is market value. INTC can't be placed.

beats.label: ENTERPRISE VALUE ÷ EBITDA
beats.title: Buying the whole company
beats.caption: Shares, plus the debt you'd take on, minus the cash in the till. Then: how many years of operating cash profit (EBITDA) that price equals.

beats.label: ALL METRICS
beats.title: The spec sheet
beats.caption: Every number on one sheet. n/m means not meaningful, usually because earnings are negative.
